text: The organization shall implement and maintain access controls in accordance with IT security policies, standards, and procedures. The organization shall manage account types including individual, shared, system, and temporary accounts. Each account shall have an assigned owner, defined access privileges, and approved authorization prior to creation. The organization shall monitor, review, and update accounts based on changes in user status, including termination or role transfer. Automated mechanisms shall be used to manage the account lifecycle, including disabling inactive and temporary accounts. The organization shall audit and track all account-related activities including creation, modification, and deletion.

The information system shall enforce access controls based on approved authorization policies. The system shall control the flow of information within and between systems in accordance with defined policies. The organization shall ensure that only authorized actions are permitted across system boundaries. The organization shall implement separation of duties to reduce the risk of misuse or fraud. Responsibilities shall be documented and assigned to appropriate individuals. Access permissions shall be structured to support separation of duties and minimize security risks.

The organization shall enforce the principle of least privilege. Users shall be granted only the access necessary to perform assigned tasks. Access to sensitive systems, configurations, and security controls shall require explicit authorization. Users with privileged access shall use non-privileged accounts when performing non-security functions. Privileged access shall be restricted to authorized personnel or roles. The system shall audit privileged actions and prevent unauthorized execution or circumvention of security controls.

The system shall enforce limits on consecutive failed login attempts within a defined time period. The system shall automatically lock accounts when the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded. Locked accounts shall remain inaccessible until released by an administrator or after a defined duration. The system shall display an approved system use notification prior to granting access. Users shall acknowledge the notification before proceeding. The notification shall inform users of monitoring, lack of privacy, and consequences of unauthorized use.

The system shall initiate a session lock after a defined period of inactivity or upon user request. The system shall require re-authentication to restore access to a locked session. The system shall conceal previously displayed information during session lock. The system shall automatically terminate user sessions after a defined period. Session management controls shall prevent unauthorized access to unattended systems.

The organization shall identify actions that may be performed without authentication and document justification for such actions. The organization shall include these exceptions in the system security plan. The organization shall define and enforce policies for remote access. Remote access shall require authorization, monitoring, and secure configuration. The system shall implement encryption to protect remote sessions. Remote access shall be routed through controlled network access points. Privileged remote access shall be limited and documented.

The organization shall define and enforce policies for wireless access. Wireless access shall require authentication and encryption. Only authorized users and devices shall be permitted to connect. The organization shall establish security requirements for mobile devices. Mobile devices shall be authorized prior to connection to the system. The organization shall enforce encryption to protect data on mobile devices.

The organization shall define terms and conditions for accessing systems from external information systems. The organization shall permit access only when required security controls are verified. External systems shall meet organizational security requirements before use. The organization shall maintain formal agreements with external entities. These agreements shall define responsibilities and security controls. The organization shall ensure that external access does not compromise internal systems.

The organization shall enforce controls for information sharing. Users shall verify that access permissions align with data restrictions before sharing information. The organization shall provide mechanisms to support secure sharing decisions. Only authorized individuals shall publish publicly accessible content. The organization shall review content prior to publication to prevent exposure of sensitive information. The organization shall conduct periodic reviews to identify and remove non-public information.

The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for violations of this policy, including termination and legal penalties. These actions shall apply to employees and external parties. The organization shall require formal requests for policy exceptions. Exception requests shall include justification, risk assessment, and mitigation measures. The organization shall define a timeline for achieving compliance. The Chief Information Officer and Chief Information Security Officer shall review and approve exception requests.

The organization shall establish and maintain rules and processes for creating, managing, and controlling digital identities to ensure secure access to applications and resources. This standard shall apply to all systems requiring authentication, including development, testing, and production environments. The organization shall implement account management processes including account creation, modification, disabling, and removal. Access to systems and resources shall be granted based on defined authorization controls. The organization shall establish and manage group and role memberships. The organization shall track and manage user accounts and associated access privileges to ensure compliance.

The organization shall define and assign roles including Information Owner, Account Manager, and, where applicable, Account Administrator and Entitlement Administrator. The organization shall document and maintain a list of authorized individuals assigned to these roles. Information Owners shall define access requirements, roles, and permissions and shall review access at least annually. Account Managers shall manage account lifecycle processes and ensure appropriate access levels. Account Administrators shall perform delegated operational tasks such as account provisioning and privilege assignment. Entitlement Administrators shall manage user privileges and support periodic access reviews.

The organization shall define and manage account types including individual, privileged, service, shared, temporary, and default accounts. Individual accounts shall be uniquely assigned to a single user. Privileged accounts shall be restricted to authorized personnel and shall follow the principle of least privilege. Access permissions shall be assigned based on job responsibilities. The organization shall ensure that all account types comply with authentication and access control standards. Account classification shall be used to enforce appropriate security controls.

The organization shall restrict administrative accounts to authorized users with appropriate identity assurance levels. Administrative account identifiers shall not reveal privilege levels. Default privileged accounts shall be disabled or renamed where possible. Default passwords shall not be used. The organization shall monitor and control the use of administrative and default accounts. Alerts shall be generated for unauthorized or suspicious login attempts.

The organization shall assign an owner to each service account responsible for its management. Service accounts shall be restricted to specific systems, devices, and usage conditions. Service accounts shall not be used for interactive login except when required for maintenance or troubleshooting. The organization shall enforce controls to ensure service accounts are used only for their intended purpose. Passwords for service accounts shall be protected and changed when personnel with knowledge of the password leave the organization.

The organization shall restrict the use of shared accounts to cases where individual accounts are not feasible. The use of shared accounts shall be documented and approved by designated authorities. The organization shall implement compensating controls to ensure accountability for shared account usage. Shared account credentials shall be updated when users no longer require access. Shared accounts shall have restricted permissions and limited access to required systems.

The organization shall disable default non-privileged accounts until required. Default non-privileged accounts shall have limited permissions and shall be subject to risk assessment before use. The organization shall enforce controls including password management and user activity logging. Emergency accounts shall be created only for urgent situations and shall bypass standard processes only when necessary. Emergency accounts shall be automatically disabled within a defined time period. The organization shall ensure proper monitoring and control of such accounts.

The organization shall create temporary accounts for short-term use with defined start and end dates. Temporary accounts shall have restricted permissions limited to required systems and functions. The organization shall enforce usage constraints including time and access conditions. Temporary accounts shall be disabled or removed after the defined period. The organization shall monitor and manage temporary account usage to prevent unauthorized access.

The organization shall implement automated mechanisms to monitor account usage and detect anomalous behavior. The system shall generate alerts based on predefined thresholds and risk levels. The organization shall notify appropriate personnel of account lifecycle events such as creation, modification, or termination. Access control policies shall enforce authorization decisions automatically. The organization shall ensure that access is denied by default unless explicitly authorized. Identity assurance levels shall define the required confidence in user identity verification.

The organization shall define identity assurance levels to determine the required confidence in user identity verification. Higher assurance levels shall require stricter authentication and access controls. The system shall enforce limits on login attempts and account lockout thresholds based on assurance level. The organization shall provide notifications for significant account events including credential changes and account status updates. Identity proofing requirements shall increase with higher assurance levels. The organization shall align security controls with the defined assurance levels.

The organization shall require valid authorization and business justification for account creation. The organization shall ensure that only authorized users or account managers modify account attributes. Access shall be granted based on the principle of least privilege. The organization shall review access rights when user roles change. Unnecessary access shall be removed promptly. The organization shall ensure proper lifecycle management of user accounts.

The organization shall disable accounts or remove access when an account poses a significant risk. The organization shall coordinate with stakeholders including information owners, account managers, legal, incident response, and human resources for timely execution. The organization shall identify and track high-risk accounts to prevent unauthorized re-enablement. Re-enabling such accounts shall require explicit approval and shall not use self-service mechanisms. The organization shall disable all user accounts immediately upon separation. Credentials shall be revoked and access attributes removed upon separation. The organization may retain access attributes for accounts disabled due to inactivity when approved by the information owner.

The organization shall require information owners to review all accounts at least annually. The organization shall review privileged account access at least every six months. The organization shall review account authorizations and access assignments at least annually. The organization shall archive accounts or associated records after defined inactivity periods or audit requirements are met. The organization shall require identity verification before unlocking user accounts using approved authentication methods. The system shall implement secure log-on procedures that prevent display of authentication tokens. The system shall display previous login information and unsuccessful login attempts upon successful authentication.

The system shall lock sessions after a maximum period of inactivity. Users shall be required to re-authenticate to regain access to locked sessions. The system shall automatically terminate sessions after a defined duration or under predefined conditions. The organization shall log, audit, and monitor all account activities in accordance with security logging standards. The organization shall restrict modification or deletion of audit records to authorized privileged accounts. The system shall ensure that all changes to access attributes are traceable to an individual. The organization shall enforce compliance with this standard and require formal exception requests for deviations.

The organization shall define authentication token requirements based on Authenticator Assurance Levels (AAL). This standard shall apply to all systems requiring authenticated access. The organization shall determine the appropriate assurance level for each system. Authentication mechanisms shall align with defined assurance levels. The organization shall implement controls for managing authentication tokens in accordance with this standard.

The organization shall define Authenticator Assurance Levels (AAL1, AAL2, AAL3) to establish identity verification requirements. AAL1 shall require single-factor or multi-factor authentication. AAL2 shall require multi-factor authentication using approved cryptographic techniques. AAL3 shall require hardware-based cryptographic authenticators and verifier impersonation resistance. The organization shall require proof of possession and control of authentication factors. The organization shall select authentication token types appropriate to the defined assurance level.

The organization shall require AAL2 authentication to include a memorized secret and a second possession-based factor. The organization shall require AAL3 authentication to include approved combinations of authentication factors. Authentication mechanisms shall use secure cryptographic protocols. The organization shall enforce the use of approved authentication combinations for each assurance level.

The organization shall implement memorized secret tokens such as passwords or PINs in accordance with defined requirements. The system shall enforce password policies including minimum length, complexity, and reuse restrictions. The system shall require password changes based on defined intervals. Temporary passwords shall be changed upon first use. The organization shall enforce multi-factor authentication where required by assurance level.

The organization shall implement look-up secret tokens as possession-based authenticators. Look-up secrets shall be securely distributed and protected. The organization shall ensure that look-up secrets meet minimum entropy requirements. Look-up secrets shall be used in accordance with defined assurance levels.

The organization shall implement out-of-band authentication tokens using separate communication channels. The system shall ensure that out-of-band tokens are transmitted securely. Email shall not be used as a transmission channel for authentication tokens. The organization shall ensure that authentication devices are uniquely associated with users.

The system shall ensure that out-of-band tokens are valid for a limited time and used only once. The system shall enforce entropy requirements for authentication secrets. The organization shall restrict use of insecure communication channels. The system shall limit failed authentication attempts for low-entropy tokens.

The organization shall implement single-factor cryptographic devices using approved cryptographic modules. The system shall ensure that cryptographic operations meet minimum entropy requirements. The organization shall use validated cryptographic standards for authentication.

The organization shall implement single-factor OTP devices for authentication. OTPs shall be generated using approved cryptographic methods. OTPs shall have a limited validity period. The system shall enforce cryptographic module validation requirements.

The organization shall implement multi-factor software cryptographic tokens requiring two authentication factors. Authentication keys shall be protected and erased after use. The system shall require activation data for each authentication. Cryptographic modules shall meet validation requirements.

The organization shall implement multi-factor OTP devices requiring a second authentication factor. OTP generation shall use approved cryptographic algorithms. Devices shall meet physical and cryptographic security requirements. The system shall enforce OTP expiration limits.

The organization shall implement multi-factor cryptographic devices requiring possession and activation factors. Authentication keys shall not be exportable. Devices shall meet defined cryptographic and physical security standards. The system shall enforce secure authentication protocols.

The organization shall enforce token expiration within a defined period. The system shall notify users prior to token expiration. Expired tokens shall be disabled automatically. The organization shall require identity verification for token renewal or re-issuance. The organization shall enforce compliance with this standard and require exception approval for deviations.

The organization shall implement encryption to protect data from unauthorized access. The organization shall apply encryption to all systems under its administrative control. Encryption mechanisms shall transform plaintext into ciphertext to ensure data confidentiality. The organization shall ensure that encryption controls are applied to systems managed internally and by third parties.

The organization shall determine encryption requirements based on data classification, risk assessment, and use case. The organization shall comply with applicable regulations and restrictions governing cryptographic technologies. The organization shall use encryption products that incorporate FIPS-approved algorithms for data at rest and in transit. The organization shall prohibit the use of outdated or insecure cryptographic algorithms. Cryptographic modules shall be FIPS 140 validated and operated in approved modes. Authentication information shall be encrypted during storage and transmission. The organization shall document encryption methodologies and product evaluations in system security plans.

The organization shall encrypt data in transit when transmitting sensitive information, including personally identifiable information. The organization shall encrypt data in transit when required by law or regulation. The organization shall require encryption for wireless network connections and remote access over public or shared networks. Public-facing systems shall use secure protocols such as HTTPS with HSTS where feasible. The organization shall implement approved encryption protocols including TLS, SSH, WPA2 or higher, and VPN technologies. The system shall disable non-compliant or weak cipher suites.

The organization shall encrypt data at rest on systems that store or process sensitive information. The organization shall require encryption for desktops, databases, mobile devices, and portable storage containing sensitive data. Full disk encryption shall be implemented on all laptops accessing organizational data. Encryption mechanisms shall use trusted hardware features such as TPM or UEFI Secure Boot. The organization shall ensure devices containing sensitive data are powered down when unattended outside secure environments. The organization shall implement mechanisms to verify encryption status of devices and storage media.

The organization shall establish controls to protect cryptographic keys. Cryptographic keys shall be securely generated, distributed, and stored. Access to cryptographic keys shall be restricted to authorized individuals. Unencrypted keys shall not be stored with the data they protect. The organization shall require key replacement upon compromise. The organization shall maintain keys and associated cryptographic systems for the duration of protected data. The organization shall enforce compliance and require formal exception approval for deviations.

The system shall uniquely identify and authenticate users and processes. The system shall implement multifactor authentication for network and local access to privileged accounts. The system shall implement multifactor authentication for non-privileged accounts where required. The system shall implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms. The system shall enforce secure authentication for remote access using cryptographic protections. The system shall accept and verify approved identity credentials.

The system shall uniquely identify and authenticate devices prior to network connection. The organization shall manage identifiers through authorized assignment processes. Identifiers shall be assigned to individuals, groups, roles, or devices as appropriate. The system shall prevent reuse of identifiers for a defined period. The system shall disable identifiers after a defined period of inactivity.

The organization shall manage authenticators through identity verification during issuance. The organization shall enforce strength requirements for authenticators. The organization shall establish procedures for distribution, revocation, and replacement of authenticators. The system shall enforce password complexity, length, and reuse restrictions. The system shall protect authenticators from unauthorized disclosure and modification. The organization shall enforce cryptographic protection for password storage and transmission. The organization shall implement controls for PKI-based authentication and certificate validation.

The system shall obscure authentication feedback to prevent information disclosure. The system shall implement authentication mechanisms for cryptographic modules in accordance with applicable standards. The system shall authenticate external users and processes. The system shall accept and verify approved third-party credentials. The organization shall use only approved identity and access management components for authentication.

The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for policy violations. These actions shall apply to employees and external parties. The organization shall require formal submission of policy exception requests. Exception requests shall include justification, risk assessment, and mitigation measures. The organization shall require approval from designated authorities for exceptions.

The organization shall classify all information and information systems. Classification shall be based on confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements. The organization shall assign impact levels based on risk to operations, assets, and individuals. The organization shall use classification to guide protection and handling of information. The organization shall review classification in alignment with business and legal requirements.

The organization shall define impact levels as low, moderate, and high. Low impact shall correspond to limited adverse effects on operations, assets, or individuals. Moderate impact shall correspond to serious adverse effects. High impact shall correspond to severe or catastrophic adverse effects. The organization shall assess impact levels based on confidentiality, integrity, and availability risks.

The organization shall classify information based on confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact levels. The organization shall define classification levels as low, moderate, and high. The organization shall evaluate the impact of unauthorized disclosure, modification, or loss of availability on operations, assets, and individuals. Low impact shall correspond to limited or no adverse effects. Moderate impact shall correspond to serious adverse effects. High impact shall correspond to severe or catastrophic adverse effects.

The organization shall implement an information classification process that includes identification, classification, and control determination. The organization shall maintain an inventory of information assets. The organization shall assign information owners and custodians. The organization shall group information assets based on risk and control requirements. The organization shall evaluate trade-offs between broad and granular classification approaches.

The organization shall assign an information owner responsible for classification and protection of information assets. The organization shall ensure a single owner is designated for each information asset. The information owner shall determine classification levels and access requirements. The organization shall assign custodians responsible for implementing controls. Custodians shall apply safeguards based on classification requirements. Third-party custodians shall operate under formal agreements defining responsibilities.

The organization shall require identification of information assets including source, purpose, dependent processes, and users. The organization shall document usage and ownership of each information asset. The organization shall identify user groups and business functions associated with information assets.

The organization shall classify information assets using confidentiality, integrity, and availability criteria. The organization shall require completion of classification assessments using approved methodologies. The organization shall involve subject matter experts where necessary. The organization shall enforce compliance with classification standards. The organization shall require formal approval for deviations through an exception process.

The organization shall restrict access to information system media to authorized personnel. The organization shall apply security markings and handling requirements to media. The organization shall store media in controlled environments. The organization shall protect media until sanitized or destroyed. The organization shall control and document media transport. The organization shall sanitize media prior to disposal or reuse. The organization shall prohibit use of unauthorized media on organizational systems.

The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for policy violations. The organization shall apply penalties to employees and external parties. The organization shall require formal exception requests including justification and risk assessment. The organization shall require approval from designated authorities for exceptions.

The organization shall implement security controls for mobile devices. The organization shall require encryption for all mobile devices accessing organizational data. The organization shall restrict applications through approved mechanisms such as whitelisting. The organization shall enforce device lock after defined inactivity periods. The organization shall implement centralized mobile device management. The organization shall monitor and update device configurations and security controls.

The organization shall allow remote access only when authorized and based on business need. The organization shall restrict access to required systems and functions. The organization shall use approved remote access methods. The organization shall require centralized authentication for remote access. Remote sessions shall require re-authentication after inactivity and shall have defined session limits. The organization shall monitor remote access activity and enforce network security controls.

The organization shall manage information throughout its lifecycle from creation to disposal. The organization shall ensure awareness of media sanitization requirements. The organization shall restrict destruction of confidential information to authorized personnel. The organization shall ensure third-party service providers comply with security requirements. The organization shall establish agreements to protect confidentiality during disposal processes.

The organization shall implement media sanitization methods including clearing, purging, and destruction. The organization shall select sanitization methods based on data confidentiality requirements. The organization shall ensure sanitized data is not recoverable. The organization shall prohibit reducing required sanitization levels. The organization shall evaluate cost and risk when selecting sanitization methods.

The organization shall maintain control over media throughout its lifecycle. The organization shall define conditions under which media is considered under or outside organizational control. The organization shall apply appropriate controls when media leaves organizational control. The organization shall evaluate reuse versus destruction based on risk and cost considerations.

The organization shall implement clearing methods to overwrite sensitive data. The organization shall ensure overwritten data is not recoverable through standard methods. The organization shall use appropriate techniques based on media type. The organization shall ensure clearing methods meet defined security objectives.

The organization shall implement purging methods to render data unrecoverable. The organization shall use techniques such as degaussing, secure erase, or destruction. The organization shall ensure purging methods meet confidentiality requirements. The organization shall avoid ineffective sanitization techniques.

The organization shall implement destruction methods to permanently eliminate data. The organization shall use approved destruction techniques such as shredding, incineration, or pulverization. The organization shall ensure data cannot be recovered using advanced techniques. The organization shall use destruction when other sanitization methods are ineffective.

The organization shall validate sanitization processes through testing and verification. The organization shall ensure sanitization tools operate effectively. The organization shall ensure personnel are trained and competent. The organization shall maintain records of sanitization activities including method and disposition. The organization shall enforce compliance and require exception approval.

The organization shall separate user and system management functionality. The system shall prevent unauthorized information transfer through shared resources. The organization shall ensure shared system resources do not expose data between users or processes.

The system shall protect against denial of service attacks. The organization shall monitor and control network boundaries. The organization shall implement boundary protection mechanisms. The system shall ensure confidentiality and integrity of transmitted data. The system shall terminate network sessions after defined conditions. The organization shall manage cryptographic keys and enforce cryptographic protections. The organization shall control collaborative devices and manage certificate trust stores.

The organization shall define and control mobile code usage. The organization shall restrict and monitor VoIP technologies. The system shall implement secure name resolution services. The organization shall ensure fault-tolerant DNS architecture. The system shall protect session authenticity. The organization shall protect information at rest. The system shall enforce process isolation. The organization shall enforce compliance with security policies.

The organization shall require all users to comply with acceptable use policies for information and IT resources. The organization shall require users to understand and adhere to information security policies and standards. The organization shall ensure users conduct activities in accordance with defined security requirements.

text: The organization shall monitor user activity on IT resources. The organization shall inform users that there is no expectation of privacy. The organization shall restrict access to IT resources based on business needs. The organization shall require authorization for access via personal devices.
policy_templates: Acceptable Use of Information Technology Resource Policy

text: Users shall comply with all applicable laws and organizational policies. Users shall protect information from unauthorized access and disclosure. Users shall use only approved IT resources. Users shall report security incidents to appropriate personnel.
policy_templates: Acceptable Use of Information Technology Resource Policy

text: The organization shall prohibit unauthorized use or disclosure of information. The organization shall prohibit use of IT resources for illegal or inappropriate activities. The organization shall restrict installation of unapproved software and devices. The organization shall prohibit circumvention of security controls.
policy_templates: Acceptable Use of Information Technology Resource Policy

text: The organization shall permit limited personal use of IT resources when it does not impact operations. The organization shall require users to maintain accountability for their credentials. The organization shall require protection of authentication credentials from unauthorized disclosure.
policy_templates: Acceptable Use of Information Technology Resource Policy

text: The organization shall prohibit transmission of sensitive information through unauthorized channels. The organization shall prohibit storage of sensitive information on unapproved devices or services. The organization shall require physical protection of devices containing organizational data. The organization shall require return of IT equipment upon request or termination.

text: The organization shall require approval for official use of social media. The organization shall restrict use of organizational accounts for official purposes only. The organization shall require protection of privileged account credentials. The organization shall prohibit unauthorized disclosure of organizational information on social media.

text: The organization shall define auditable events. The system shall generate audit records for defined events. The organization shall review and update audit requirements periodically. The system shall ensure audit records contain sufficient detail. The organization shall allocate storage for audit records.

The system shall respond to audit failures appropriately. The organization shall review and analyze audit logs. The organization shall integrate audit processes with incident response. The system shall protect audit data from unauthorized access. The organization shall restrict audit access to authorized users.

The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for policy violations, including termination and legal penalties. The organization shall apply penalties to employees and non-employees. The organization shall require formal submission of policy exception requests. Exception requests shall include justification, risk assessment, mitigation measures, and a defined compliance timeline. The Chief Information Officer and Chief Information Security Officer shall review and approve exception requests.

The organization shall develop, document, and maintain baseline configurations for information systems. The organization shall review and update baseline configurations periodically and upon significant system changes. The organization shall retain previous versions of baseline configurations to support rollback. The organization shall define and control configuration changes. The organization shall review, approve, and document configuration changes based on security impact analysis. The organization shall test and validate changes prior to implementation.

The organization shall define and enforce access restrictions for system changes. The organization shall establish and implement secure configuration settings. The organization shall approve and document deviations from baseline configurations. The organization shall configure systems to provide only essential functionality. The organization shall disable unnecessary ports, services, and protocols. The organization shall maintain an inventory of system components and detect unauthorized components. The organization shall implement configuration management plans and enforce software usage restrictions.

The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for policy violations. The organization shall require formal exception requests including justification, risk assessment, and mitigation measures. The organization shall require approval from designated authorities for exceptions. The organization shall assign responsibility for policy enforcement to the Chief Information Office.

The organization shall develop and maintain contingency plans for information systems. The organization shall identify critical business functions and recovery requirements. The organization shall define recovery objectives and restoration priorities. The organization shall assign roles and responsibilities for contingency operations. The organization shall review and update contingency plans periodically. The organization shall protect contingency plans from unauthorized access.

The organization shall provide contingency training to personnel based on assigned roles. The organization shall test contingency plans at least annually. The organization shall review test results and implement corrective actions. The organization shall establish alternate storage sites for backup data. The organization shall ensure alternate sites provide equivalent security controls. The organization shall document risks and mitigation strategies for alternate site accessibility.

The organization shall establish an alternate processing site to support resumption of critical operations within defined recovery time and recovery point objectives. The organization shall ensure required equipment, supplies, and contractual arrangements are available to support transfer of operations. The alternate processing site shall provide security safeguards equivalent to the primary site. The organization shall ensure geographic separation between primary and alternate sites to reduce common risk exposure. The organization shall identify accessibility risks to the alternate site and define mitigation strategies. The organization shall establish service agreements with priority-of-service provisions aligned to business requirements. The organization shall implement alternate telecommunications services to ensure continuity of operations. Telecommunications service agreements shall include priority-of-service provisions and support recovery objectives.

The organization shall perform backups of user-level, system-level, and security-related information in accordance with defined recovery objectives. Backup frequency shall align with recovery time and recovery point objectives. The organization shall protect backup data to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability. The organization shall test backup media to verify reliability and data integrity. The organization shall implement recovery and reconstitution processes to restore systems to a known secure state after disruption or failure. Transaction-based systems shall support transaction recovery mechanisms. The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for policy violations. The organization shall require formal exception requests including justification, risk assessment, mitigation measures, and defined timelines, subject to approval by the CIO and CISO.

The organization shall establish and maintain an information security policy that defines minimum security requirements. The organization shall protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and infrastructure assets. The organization shall manage risks related to information security threats and vulnerabilities. The organization shall monitor systems for anomalies and respond to incidents involving misuse, loss, or unauthorized disclosure of information. The organization shall promote information security awareness across all users. The organization shall implement controls to ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements. The organization shall ensure personnel understand their responsibilities in protecting organizational information.

The organization shall apply this policy to all information systems, including those managed by third parties. The organization shall implement both risk management and technical security functions. The organization shall designate responsible roles for risk management and information security functions. The organization shall ensure security decisions consider enterprise-wide risk and business objectives. The organization shall ensure technical security functions evaluate and advise on security risks. The organization shall require consultation between risk management and security functions for decision-making. The organization shall retain accountability for information security even when services are outsourced.

Executive management shall evaluate and accept organizational risk. Executive management shall define and integrate security responsibilities into business processes. Executive management shall allocate resources and support implementation of security policies. Executive management shall promote security awareness and best practices. Executive management shall ensure implementation of information classification and data handling processes. Executive management shall assign information ownership and maintain accountability for data protection. Executive management shall participate in incident response and ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.

The Information Security Officer shall maintain knowledge of business functions and security requirements. The Information Security Officer shall maintain professional competency through ongoing education. The Information Security Officer shall assess compliance with policies and regulatory requirements. The Information Security Officer shall evaluate and manage security risks. The Information Security Officer shall provide guidance on security architecture and procurement decisions. The Information Security Officer shall escalate unresolved security concerns. The Information Security Officer shall disseminate threat intelligence and support incident response. The Information Security Officer shall promote security awareness and support policy development.

IT management shall implement and maintain security controls within infrastructure and networks. IT management shall allocate resources to maintain required security levels. IT management shall implement policies, processes, and controls based on business and regulatory requirements. IT management shall enforce controls based on information classification. IT management shall provide training for secure operations. IT management shall support identification and implementation of appropriate security controls. IT management shall implement business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities. The workforce shall protect information from unauthorized use or disclosure. The workforce shall comply with acceptable use policies and report security incidents to appropriate personnel.

The Chief Information Security Officer shall provide security expertise and consultation. The Chief Information Security Officer shall develop and maintain the enterprise security program, strategy, and effectiveness measures. The Chief Information Security Officer shall establish and maintain security policies and standards. The Chief Information Security Officer shall assess compliance with security policies and standards. The Chief Information Security Officer shall provide guidance on secure system engineering. The Chief Information Security Officer shall coordinate incident response activities. The Chief Information Security Officer shall monitor networks and external sources for security threats and vulnerabilities. The Chief Information Security Officer shall maintain communication with security organizations and authorities. The Chief Information Security Officer shall provide timely threat intelligence and security awareness resources. The organization shall implement separation of duties to reduce risk of misuse. Where separation of duties is not feasible, compensating controls including monitoring, audit trails, and supervision shall be implemented. Audit and approval functions shall remain independent from implementation of controls.

The organization shall perform information security risk assessments at least annually and during system development lifecycle events including new systems, major changes, and identified vulnerabilities. Risk assessment methodologies shall align with legal, regulatory, and organizational requirements. Risk assessment results and decisions shall be documented. The organization shall ensure all information assets are assigned an owner and used only for authorized business purposes. The organization shall classify information based on confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Information shall be classified at the highest required level based on data sensitivity, including classification of merged data sets. The organization shall apply baseline controls aligned to classification levels. The organization shall maintain an inventory of information assets. The organization shall establish processes for secure handling, sharing, and external release of non-public information, including documentation of responsibilities, controls, compliance, and approvals. Personally identifiable information shall be protected with appropriate safeguards.

The organization shall assign ownership of all IT assets to designated individuals or business units. The organization shall maintain an inventory of hardware and software assets with sufficient granularity for tracking and reporting. Asset inventories shall be automated where feasible. The organization shall implement processes including regular scanning to detect unauthorized hardware and software. The organization shall provide security awareness training to personnel within defined timelines and reinforce training annually. The organization shall ensure users acknowledge acceptable use policies. The organization shall perform suitability checks for personnel with access to sensitive systems where permitted. The organization shall periodically review suitability determinations. The organization shall ensure return of organizational assets and immediate removal of access upon employee separation.

The organization shall establish and maintain an incident response plan. The organization shall require prompt reporting of security incidents and weaknesses. The organization shall ensure escalation of unresolved concerns to appropriate authorities. The organization shall notify the Security Operations Center for significant incidents and ensure coordinated response. The organization shall define and enforce physical security perimeters and access controls for facilities. The organization shall conduct periodic risk assessments of facilities. The organization shall protect IT equipment from environmental and security threats. The organization shall escort visitors in secure areas. The organization shall ensure protection of information media based on classification.

The organization shall assign responsibility for account management. The system shall enforce unique user identification and authentication mechanisms. The system shall implement session locking and re-authentication after inactivity. The system shall terminate sessions based on defined conditions. Authentication tokens shall be protected as confidential and stored securely. Access shall be granted based on least privilege and job responsibilities. Privileged users shall use separate non-privileged accounts for routine activities. Systems shall display logon banners informing users of monitoring and lack of privacy. Remote access shall require prior authorization, risk assessment, and secure connection through managed entry points. Remote work shall require defined data protection practices.

The organization shall assign responsibility for system administration. Systems shall be developed and maintained in accordance with secure system development lifecycle practices. Systems shall implement controls aligned with data classification. Systems shall synchronize time with authoritative time sources. Systems shall be tested prior to deployment. The organization shall enforce separation of environments including development, testing, and production. The organization shall implement formal change management processes. Software shall follow secure coding practices. Test data shall be protected in accordance with classification. Production data used for testing shall be controlled, masked, or removed after use. Development tools and source code shall not be maintained on production systems where feasible. Network connections shall be authorized, documented, and periodically reviewed. Network architecture shall enforce segmentation. Authentication shall be required for all users and devices. Network monitoring shall be restricted to authorized personnel.

Collaborative devices shall prohibit remote activation and provide clear indication of use. The organization shall require vulnerability scanning prior to production deployment and periodically thereafter. Critical systems shall undergo periodic penetration testing. Vulnerability assessments shall be coordinated with third parties where applicable. Scan results shall be reviewed and shared with security authorities. The organization shall remediate vulnerabilities through defined action plans and milestones. Vulnerability testing shall be conducted only by authorized personnel. Unauthorized testing shall be treated as a security violation.

The organization shall define and document operational procedures and responsibilities. Systems shall follow approved configuration standards. The organization shall monitor system capacity and ensure resource availability. Host-based firewalls shall be implemented. The organization shall implement controls to prevent and detect malicious code. Automatic execution from removable media shall be restricted. The organization shall restrict data storage to authorized locations. Systems shall allow only approved software to execute. Systems shall be maintained at vendor-supported levels. Security patches shall be applied in a timely and automated manner where feasible. Unsupported systems shall be removed. Systems shall generate and protect audit logs. Monitoring systems shall detect and alert on security events. The organization shall establish and test contingency plans. The organization shall define system criticality, recovery objectives, and backup requirements. Backup and restoration processes shall be tested. Separation of duties shall be enforced. Compensating controls shall be implemented when necessary.

The organization shall enforce compliance with all policies and standards. Policies may be updated and compliance with updated versions shall be required. The organization shall require formal exception requests when compliance is not feasible. Exception requests shall be reviewed and approved through the Chief Information Security Officer’s process.

The organization shall maintain IT resources in compliance with security policies, standards, and procedures. The IT Department shall schedule, perform, document, and review maintenance and repair activities in accordance with vendor requirements. The IT Department shall approve and monitor all maintenance activities, including on-site and remote maintenance. System owners shall approve removal of systems or components for off-site maintenance. The organization shall sanitize equipment prior to off-site maintenance. The organization shall verify security controls after maintenance activities. Maintenance records shall include relevant system and activity details. Maintenance tools shall be approved, controlled, and inspected for unauthorized modifications. Diagnostic media shall be scanned for malicious code before use.

The IT Department shall approve and monitor nonlocal maintenance activities. Nonlocal maintenance shall be permitted only when documented in the system security plan. The organization shall use strong authentication for remote maintenance sessions. The organization shall maintain records of nonlocal maintenance activities. Sessions and network connections shall be terminated after completion. The organization shall define and document nonlocal maintenance procedures. The organization shall authorize maintenance personnel and maintain an approved list. Maintenance personnel shall have appropriate access authorization or be supervised. The organization shall ensure timely maintenance support in accordance with service level agreements.

The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for policy violations, including termination and legal penalties. These actions shall apply to employees and non-employees. The organization shall require formal exception requests including scope, justification, risk assessment, mitigation measures, and timelines. Exception requests shall be reviewed and approved by the Chief Information Security Officer and Chief Information Officer.

The organization shall apply personnel security safeguards to IT resource access. The organization shall assign risk designations to positions and establish screening criteria. Personnel shall be screened prior to access authorization and rescreened as required. Screening shall comply with applicable laws and policies. Upon termination, access shall be revoked, credentials disabled, and organizational assets retrieved. Exit processes shall include security awareness and accountability. The organization shall notify relevant personnel of termination events and enforce post-employment security requirements.

The organization shall review and update access authorizations upon personnel transfer. Access rights shall be modified based on job responsibilities. The organization shall notify relevant personnel of transfers. The organization shall establish and maintain access agreements, including acknowledgment prior to granting access. Access agreements shall be reviewed and revalidated periodically. The organization shall define personnel security requirements for third parties. Third parties shall comply with organizational security policies and notify personnel changes. The organization shall monitor third-party compliance.

The organization shall implement a formal sanction process for policy violations. The organization shall notify relevant personnel when sanctions are initiated. Sanctions shall comply with legal and regulatory requirements. The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for employees and non-employees. The organization shall require formal exception requests including justification, risk, mitigation, and timelines. Exception requests shall be reviewed and approved by designated authorities.

The organization shall implement physical security controls to prevent unauthorized access and damage. The organization shall maintain an authorized access list and issue access credentials. Access shall be reviewed and revoked when no longer required. The organization shall enforce access control at entry and exit points. The organization shall maintain access logs and monitor physical access. Visitors shall be escorted and monitored. Physical access devices shall be secured, inventoried, and updated periodically.

The organization shall perform facility penetration testing to evaluate physical security controls. The organization shall control access to transmission media and output devices. The organization shall monitor physical access and review logs regularly. The organization shall maintain visitor access records and review them periodically. Physical access monitoring shall integrate with incident response processes.

The organization shall protect power equipment and cabling from damage. The organization shall implement emergency power shutdown capabilities. Emergency power supplies shall support orderly shutdown and continued operations. The organization shall implement emergency lighting for critical areas and evacuation routes. Emergency systems shall be protected from unauthorized use.

The organization shall implement fire detection and suppression systems. The organization shall maintain environmental controls including temperature and humidity monitoring. The organization shall protect systems from water damage. The organization shall control and monitor delivery and removal of equipment. Physical protections shall align with system criticality and environmental risks.

The organization shall implement security controls for alternate work sites. The organization shall assess effectiveness of controls at alternate locations. The organization shall provide communication channels for reporting security incidents. The organization shall enforce compliance and disciplinary actions. The organization shall require formal exception approval for deviations.

The organization shall develop and maintain system security plans. Security plans shall define system boundaries, operational context, and security categorization. Security plans shall document security requirements and controls. Plans shall be reviewed, approved, and updated periodically. The organization shall distribute plans to authorized personnel. Security plans shall be protected from unauthorized access and modification.

The organization shall establish rules of behavior for system users. Users shall acknowledge and agree to rules prior to access. The organization shall review and update rules periodically. Users shall re-acknowledge rules upon updates to maintain access.

The organization shall develop and maintain an information security architecture that defines the protection of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information. The architecture shall be integrated with and support the enterprise architecture. The organization shall document assumptions and dependencies on external services. The organization shall review and update the security architecture at least annually. Changes to the security architecture shall be reflected in system security plans, operations, and acquisition processes. The organization shall implement a defense-in-depth approach by allocating security controls across multiple layers and ensuring controls operate in a coordinated and reinforcing manner.

The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for policy violations, including termination and legal penalties. The organization shall apply penalties to employees and non-employees. The organization shall require formal exception requests including scope, justification, risk assessment, mitigation measures, and timelines. Exception requests shall be reviewed and approved by the Chief Information Security Officer and Chief Information Officer. The organization shall assign responsibility for compliance to the Chief Information Office and system owners.

The organization shall integrate information security requirements into all phases of the system development life cycle. The organization shall identify and address system requirements early to prevent delays, cost overruns, and inadequate system design. The organization shall ensure security controls are incorporated throughout development to mitigate risks such as data breaches, system compromise, and legal or financial impacts.

text: The organization shall implement a secure system development life cycle for all systems and applications. The organization shall define and document security roles and responsibilities. The organization shall classify information and determine system criticality. The organization shall assess threats, vulnerabilities, and risks. The organization shall select, implement, and document security controls. The organization shall test and validate security controls and perform certification and accreditation. The organization shall manage changes, monitor compliance, and securely dispose of systems. The organization shall document all security activities and retain records for auditing. The organization shall apply security controls proportionate to system risk and classification, and document and approve any deviations through formal risk acceptance processes.

text: The organization shall enforce compliance with all policies and standards. The organization shall comply with updated policies and standards upon revision. The organization shall require formal exception requests when compliance is not feasible. Exception requests shall be reviewed and approved through the Chief Information Security Officer’s process. The organization shall align risk assessments and controls with recognized standards.
