text: The organization shall provide information security awareness training to all users. The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for violations. The organization shall require formal exception requests including justification, risk, mitigation, and timelines. Exception requests shall be reviewed and approved by the Chief Information Security Officer and Chief Information Officer.

The organization shall provide initial and periodic security awareness training. Training shall include understanding of security responsibilities, incident reporting, and operational security. The organization shall provide training on insider threat detection and reporting. The organization shall provide role-based security training prior to system access and periodically thereafter. The organization shall provide training on physical and environmental controls. The organization shall conduct practical security exercises such as simulated attacks. The organization shall train personnel to identify suspicious communications and anomalous behavior. The organization shall document and retain training records.

The organization shall ensure that systems and services are acquired with defined security requirements aligned with mission and business objectives. The organization shall enforce compliance and disciplinary actions for violations. The organization shall require formal exception requests subject to approval by the Chief Information Security Officer and Chief Information Officer.

The organization shall define and allocate resources for information security during planning and budgeting processes. The organization shall integrate information security into the system development life cycle. The organization shall define security roles and responsibilities. The organization shall integrate risk management into development activities. The organization shall include security requirements in acquisition processes, including functional, assurance, documentation, and acceptance criteria. The organization shall ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and standards.

The organization shall define and document security control requirements and system design specifications. The organization shall identify required ports, protocols, and services early in the development life cycle. The organization shall use approved identity verification products where applicable. The organization shall obtain and protect system documentation including administrator and user guidance. Documentation shall include secure configuration, operation, vulnerabilities, and user responsibilities. The organization shall restrict access to documentation to authorized personnel.

The organization shall apply security engineering principles throughout system design, development, and implementation. The organization shall require external service providers to comply with security requirements. The organization shall define roles and responsibilities for external services. The organization shall monitor compliance of external providers. The organization shall require identification of required services, ports, and protocols for external systems.

The organization shall require developers to implement configuration management for systems and components. Developers shall document and control changes and assess security impacts. Developers shall track and remediate security flaws. The organization shall ensure integrity verification of software, firmware, and hardware. The organization shall implement tools to compare system versions and maintain integrity of build data. The organization shall ensure updates match approved configurations.

The organization shall require developers to implement security testing and evaluation processes. Developers shall perform unit, integration, system, and regression testing. Developers shall produce evidence of testing and implement flaw remediation processes. The organization shall require static and dynamic code analysis. The organization shall perform threat and vulnerability assessments. The organization shall require independent verification of testing results. The organization shall perform manual code reviews and penetration testing. The organization shall ensure testing coverage for all security controls.

The organization shall implement patch management processes to remediate vulnerabilities through software and firmware updates. The organization shall apply patches to all applicable systems. The organization shall follow vulnerability management standards for non-patchable vulnerabilities. The organization shall enforce compliance and require formal exception approval for deviations.

The organization shall assign responsibility for patch management. The organization shall implement a patch management process including monitoring vulnerabilities, testing patches, and deploying updates. The organization shall use centralized automated patch management tools where feasible. The organization shall enforce separation of duties in patch deployment and verification. The organization shall prioritize patching based on vulnerability severity. The organization shall adhere to defined patch timelines and implement compensating controls where timelines are not met.

The organization shall establish secure baseline configurations for all systems. The organization shall apply secure configurations to all systems unless technically infeasible. The organization shall require formal exception approval for deviations.

The organization shall implement secure configuration baselines based on industry standards and vendor guidance. The organization shall document and approve configuration changes. The organization shall perform configuration changes through formal change management processes. The organization shall maintain configuration management plans. The organization shall monitor systems for misconfigurations and unauthorized changes.

The organization shall generate and manage security logs. The organization shall protect logs as sensitive information. The organization shall enforce compliance and require exception approval for deviations.

The organization shall generate logs for all systems and components. The organization shall log security events with sufficient detail. The organization shall implement real-time alerting for log failures. The organization shall centralize log collection. The organization shall retain logs for defined durations. The organization shall restrict access to log data and monitor usage.

The organization shall implement system integrity monitoring. The organization shall enforce disciplinary actions for policy violations. The organization shall require formal exception approval for deviations.

The organization shall identify, report, and remediate system flaws. The organization shall test updates prior to deployment. The organization shall install updates within defined timeframes. The organization shall implement malicious code protection mechanisms. The organization shall perform periodic and real-time scans. The organization shall respond to malicious code detection appropriately.

The organization shall monitor systems for attacks and unauthorized activity. The organization shall deploy monitoring tools and protect monitoring data. The organization shall adjust monitoring levels based on risk. The organization shall disseminate alerts to authorized personnel. The organization shall ensure alerts trigger appropriate response actions.

The organization shall receive and disseminate security alerts and advisories. The organization shall implement integrity verification mechanisms. The organization shall detect unauthorized changes to systems. The organization shall implement spam protection mechanisms. The organization shall centrally manage protection systems.

The system shall validate input data. The system shall restrict manual overrides to authorized users and audit usage. The system shall handle errors securely without exposing sensitive information. The organization shall enforce information handling and retention policies. The system shall implement memory protection mechanisms.

The organization shall implement vulnerability management processes. The organization shall track, evaluate, and remediate vulnerabilities. The organization shall enforce compliance and require exception approval for deviations.

The organization shall perform vulnerability scans on all systems. The organization shall classify scan types based on system type and exposure. The organization shall conduct infrastructure, application, and source code scans.

The organization shall use approved vulnerability scanning tools. The organization shall ensure scan coverage for all systems. The organization shall protect scan reports. The organization shall perform scans during development and operational phases.

The organization shall perform pre-deployment vulnerability scans. The organization shall remediate vulnerabilities prior to deployment. The organization shall require formal approval for systems with unremediated vulnerabilities.

The organization shall perform implementation and recurring vulnerability scans. The organization shall determine scan frequency based on system risk rating. The organization shall remediate all identified vulnerabilities.

The organization shall determine risk ratings based on impact and exposure. The organization shall use classification to guide scanning frequency. Systems without risk ratings shall be treated as high risk.

The organization shall perform scans at defined frequencies based on risk rating. The organization shall remediate vulnerabilities within defined timeframes. The organization shall verify remediation. The organization shall report unremediated vulnerabilities to management.

Define responsibilities for responding to security threats impacting confidentiality, integrity, and availability of IT resources. Establish enforcement mechanisms with disciplinary actions for policy violations applicable to employees and external parties. Apply contractual and access restrictions for non-compliant third parties. Implement a formal exception management process requiring documented justification, risk impact analysis, and mitigation measures. Require executive review and approval of all exception requests. Ensure exceptions include defined timelines and actions to achieve compliance.

Establish a centralized Computer Emergency Response Team (CCERT) led by designated leadership to coordinate incident response activities. Require each department to form a Departmental Computer Emergency Response Team (DCERT) to manage localized incident response. Define roles, responsibilities, and communication protocols between CCERT and DCERT teams. Implement procedures for incident handling, reporting, external communication, and coordination with stakeholders. Maintain updated contact information and ensure availability of communication tools for response personnel. Ensure timely reporting, evidence preservation, and coordination with legal or external authorities when required.

Establish a standardized incident response process defining roles, responsibilities, and stakeholder involvement. Define incident categories, severity levels, and triggering conditions to support consistent response actions. Implement procedures for incident detection, notification, evidence handling, containment, and recovery. Ensure collection of accurate incident data and reporting to support decision-making. Conduct regular testing, lessons learned activities, and metric collection to evaluate response effectiveness. Maintain compliance with organizational policies and update processes as required.

Define and document roles and responsibilities for all incident response stakeholders to ensure coordinated response activities. Assign leadership roles such as CISO for overall incident response coordination and escalation. Establish a Security Operations Center to handle detection, analysis, response, and reporting of incidents. Require technical staff to support response activities and ensure forensic analysis is conducted by authorized personnel. Include executive, legal, and communication teams in incident response planning and execution. Enable collaboration with external entities for investigation, response support, and threat intelligence sharing.

Establish a structured incident response process beginning with preparation activities to ensure readiness. Maintain updated contact lists, communication channels, and defined roles for incident reporting and coordination. Develop and enforce standard operating procedures aligned with industry best practices. Conduct regular testing of incident response capabilities using realistic scenarios and exercises. Require all personnel to report suspected incidents to designated security representatives. Continuously update processes based on lessons learned and evolving threats.

Implement processes to identify and analyze anomalies to determine the occurrence and nature of security incidents. Assign responsibility for incident classification, prioritization, and escalation based on severity. Define incident categories and severity levels to support consistent response decisions. Ensure incidents are promptly escalated to appropriate stakeholders for coordinated action. Use classification frameworks to prioritize response activities and resource allocation. Continuously refine categorization as investigations progress.

Define standardized incident categories and severity levels to classify and prioritize security incidents. Categorize incidents based on type, including unauthorized access, denial of service, malicious code, and improper usage. Establish severity levels based on business impact to guide response actions. Ensure incident classification supports timely and appropriate response measures. Allow reclassification as new information becomes available during investigation. Use classification and severity frameworks to improve incident management consistency and efficiency.

Establish formal escalation procedures to ensure timely and effective communication during incidents. Define escalation matrices, contact lists, and communication channels for all stakeholders. Ensure rapid notification without delaying containment and response actions. Maintain up-to-date contact information with alternate communication options. Enable coordinated communication across internal and external stakeholders. Ensure accurate and timely dissemination of incident information to support response activities.

Define processes for initial incident scoping to identify affected systems and potential impact areas. Establish criteria for identifying targets, external connections, and threat scenarios. Use verified evidence sources to support accurate scoping decisions. Limit scope appropriately to avoid excessive data and resource usage. Continuously refine scope as new information becomes available during investigation. Ensure scoping considers operational constraints and resource limitations.

Implement a centralized incident tracking system with controlled access to support response activities. Record key incident details including timestamps, type, status, actions taken, and involved parties. Maintain documentation of evidence collected during investigations. Ensure records support audit requirements and potential legal proceedings. Provide visibility into incident progress and next steps. Maintain comprehensive logs to support analysis and continuous improvement.

Implement containment procedures to limit the spread and impact of security incidents. Identify all affected systems and isolate compromised components to prevent further damage. Apply containment measures such as blocking malicious activity and disabling affected services. Collect relevant information during containment to support analysis and remediation. Adjust containment strategies based on incident severity and operational risk. Ensure leadership oversight in decision-making for containment actions.

Implement eradication processes to remove threats from affected systems using appropriate technical measures. Conduct iterative analysis during containment and eradication to ensure complete threat removal. Restore systems through secure recovery processes using trusted images and clean backups. Validate that restored systems are free from vulnerabilities before returning to operation. Apply system hardening and enhanced monitoring to prevent recurrence. Require formal validation and certification that the incident has been resolved.

Conduct post-incident reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of incident response activities and identify process improvements. Document response actions, root cause analysis, and identified weaknesses for each incident. Use lessons learned to update incident response procedures, training programs, and technical controls. Implement proactive measures such as testing, vulnerability assessments, and policy reviews to prevent recurrence. Maintain a centralized repository of incident reports and lessons learned for future reference. Share findings with stakeholders to enhance awareness and strengthen incident response capabilities.

Establish and maintain incident response metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of response activities. Collect and report metrics for each incident to support organizational situational awareness. Track incident volume, types, resolution time, resource utilization, and system downtime. Measure financial impact, including costs related to containment, recovery, and investigation. Monitor damage indicators such as affected systems and compromised records. Use forensic metrics and trend analysis to identify gaps, support decision-making, and justify resource allocation.

Establish an incident response capability to identify, contain, investigate, remediate, and report security incidents. Ensure all personnel comply with incident response policies and enforce disciplinary actions for violations. Apply contractual and access restrictions for non-compliant external parties. Define a formal exception management process requiring documented justification, risk impact analysis, and mitigation measures. Require executive review and approval of policy exceptions. Ensure exceptions include defined timelines and actions to achieve compliance.

Provide role-based incident response training within defined timeframes and update it regularly to address system changes. Conduct simulated exercises and use automated tools to enhance training effectiveness. Test incident response capabilities periodically and document results to evaluate performance. Implement a structured incident handling process covering detection, analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery. Establish mechanisms for incident monitoring, reporting, and coordination with related continuity plans. Maintain and regularly update an incident response plan, ensuring secure distribution, approval, and protection from unauthorized access.

Implement a risk management framework to identify, analyze, and manage risks to confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Conduct regular risk assessments to prioritize risks affecting critical information assets. Align security practices with business objectives and regulatory requirements. Integrate risk considerations early in system design to reduce future remediation costs. Use assessment results to inform decision-making and improve security posture. Enforce compliance requirements and manage exceptions through a formal approval process.

Implement risk management processes that evaluate vulnerabilities, threats, and existing security controls to determine risk levels. Conduct various assessment activities such as audits, reviews, and vulnerability testing to identify risks. Ensure all systems and processes supporting business functions undergo risk assessments throughout their lifecycle. Recognize that risks cannot be fully eliminated and must be actively managed. Use assessment results to improve overall security posture and control effectiveness. Maintain continuous evaluation of risks to support informed security decisions.

Establish an iterative risk management process integrated across the system lifecycle. Define risk assessment strategies, including assumptions, constraints, and resource considerations. Determine organizational risk tolerance at the executive level and ensure alignment across entities. Identify and classify assets, threats, and vulnerabilities to assess risk likelihood and impact. Conduct comprehensive risk assessments proportional to system criticality and data sensitivity. Support risk assessments with documented methodologies and predefined assessment types.

Define and implement risk response strategies based on assessed risk levels and organizational tolerance. Document risk acceptance decisions with justification and ensure alignment with risk tolerance. Apply risk avoidance by eliminating high-risk activities or technologies when necessary. Implement risk mitigation controls to reduce risks to acceptable levels. Use risk transfer mechanisms such as outsourcing or contractual agreements where appropriate. Ensure all risk response actions are formally documented and reviewed.

Monitor the effectiveness of implemented risk response measures to ensure controls operate as intended. Conduct periodic reviews of risk management activities at least annually. Establish mechanisms to detect significant changes in risk factors such as threats, assets, and controls. Trigger reassessment when changes impact the organization’s risk posture. Ensure continuous alignment of risk management practices with evolving conditions. Maintain documentation to support monitoring and reassessment activities.

Ensure risk assessments are conducted in compliance with defined security policies, standards, and procedures. Enforce disciplinary actions for policy violations applicable to employees and external parties. Apply contractual and access restrictions for non-compliant third parties. Establish a formal exception management process requiring documented justification, risk analysis, and mitigation measures. Require executive review and approval of all exceptions. Define timelines and corrective actions to achieve compliance with policy requirements.

Apply appropriate security controls to data classified as confidential, including PHI and PII, in compliance with applicable laws and standards. Document all implemented security controls and their rationale within the system security plan. Conduct formal risk assessments to evaluate the likelihood and impact of threats to information systems and data. Record risk assessment results annually, review them quarterly, and communicate findings to relevant stakeholders. Update risk assessments regularly or upon significant system or environmental changes. Perform periodic vulnerability scans, analyze results, remediate identified vulnerabilities within defined timelines, and ensure continuous updates to scanning tools and definitions.

Ensure implementation of security controls across information systems and their environments throughout the system lifecycle, including authorization, assessment, and continuous monitoring. Integrate security requirements into system development and operational processes. Enforce compliance through defined disciplinary actions for violations applicable to employees and external parties. Apply contractual and access restrictions for non-compliant third parties. Establish a formal exception management process requiring documented justification, risk impact analysis, and mitigation strategies. Require executive review and approval of exceptions with defined timelines for achieving compliance.

Develop and maintain a documented security assessment and authorization policy outlining roles, responsibilities, scope, and compliance requirements. Establish procedures to support consistent implementation of assessment and authorization controls. Periodically review and update policies and procedures to ensure continued effectiveness. Create a formal security assessment plan defining scope, controls, methodologies, and responsible personnel. Conduct assessments to verify that controls are properly implemented, functioning as intended, and meeting security requirements. Document assessment results and communicate findings to designated stakeholders.

Authorize system interconnections through formal agreements that define security requirements and data exchange characteristics. Document all interconnections, including interfaces, security controls, and information types shared. Regularly review and update interconnection agreements to maintain security alignment. Implement controlled connection policies to regulate external system access based on defined rules. Develop and maintain a plan of action and milestones to address identified security weaknesses and vulnerabilities. Assign an authorizing official to approve system operation and ensure periodic updates to system authorization status.

Establish and implement a continuous monitoring strategy with defined metrics, assessment frequencies, and monitoring processes. Perform ongoing assessments of security controls to evaluate effectiveness and detect deviations. Continuously monitor system security status and analyze collected data for risk indicators. Correlate security information to support timely response actions and risk mitigation. Report security status to designated stakeholders at defined intervals. Authorize and document internal system connections, ensuring defined security requirements and controlled data exchange.
